question: The cracker-like smell of fresh bread crust comes mainly from one molecule. What else is scented by it?
answer: Basmati rice. The molecule, 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline, forms in the hot crust when the amino acid proline meets fragments of sugar, so sugar alone cannot make it. The nose detects it at about a tenth of a millionth of a gram per litre of water. Pandan leaves and fresh popcorn owe their scent to it too.
move: A smell is a molecule, and one molecule can turn up in many foods.
trap: Crediting browned sugar, the flavour everyone links with browning.
source: Schieberle & Grosch, Z. Lebensm. Unters. Forsch., 1987
reference: Schieberle & Grosch, Evaluation of the flavour of wheat and rye bread crusts by aroma extract dilution analysis, Zeitschrift für Lebensmittel-Untersuchung und -Forschung, 1987
